issues.legal_issue: A state legislature is competent to impose a surcharge that enhances land revenue.
material_facts: The legislation imposed a surcharge on existing land revenue and provided for its recovery as land revenue.
The surcharge was increased for certain classes of land, but remained an addition to the land revenue.
issues.conclusion: The surcharge was an enhancement of land revenue, not a tax on land revenue, and the state legislature was competent to enact it.
issues.legal_principle: The levy fell within Entry 45 of List II because its substance was enhanced land revenue; increasing the surcharge, even substantially, did not change its character. The Court agreed with C. V. Rajagopalachariar v. State of Madras, AIR 1960 Mad 543. It also noted that Article 271 describes a surcharge as an increase in specified duties or taxes.

predicates.challenge_to_state_legislative_competenc: A party challenged whether a state legislature had authority to enact a levy on land revenue.
predicates.surcharge_added_to_existing_land_revenue: The legislature imposed an additional charge calculated by reference to existing land revenue.
predicates.surcharge_recovered_as_land_revenue: The additional charge was treated and recovered as land revenue.

issues.definition: When a challenge to legislative competence concerns an additional charge on existing land revenue that is recovered as land revenue, the rule permits the state legislature to impose that charge as land revenue.

issues.legal_issue: Temporary regional differences in land-revenue burdens do not violate the constitutional equality guarantee when they arise during state reorganisation and pending uniform resettlement and survey.
material_facts: After state reorganisation, land revenue in different regions continued to be assessed under differing existing settlements and laws.
The challenged surcharge operated as a temporary measure while survey and resettlement were underway across the state to establish a uniform land-revenue system.
The surcharge was imposed on the existing assessments, and the resulting burdens differed between regions.
issues.conclusion: The temporary surcharge did not violate the constitutional equality guarantee despite differences in taxation between regions.
issues.legal_principle: A classification must rest on an intelligible differentia and that differentia must have a rational relation to the statute's object, as stated in State of Andhra Pradesh v. Nalla Raja Reddy, [1967] 3 SCR 28. Temporary reliance on existing regional assessments while a uniform system is being developed may be justified during reorganisation; continuing regional differences for that purpose is not, by itself, discriminatory. The Court relied on State of Madhya Pradesh v. Bhopal Sugar Industries Ltd., [1964] 6 SCR 846, and referred to the reasoning in C. V. Rajagopalachariar v. State of Madras, AIR 1960 Mad 543. It also noted that no definite time limit can be prescribed for making the adjustments needed to achieve uniformity.

predicates.equality_challenge_to_land_revenue_levy: A party challenged a land-revenue levy on the ground that its effects differed between regions.
predicates.regional_assessments_were_inherited_afte: After the state was reorganised, different regions continued to use their existing land-revenue assessments.
predicates.levy_was_temporary: The legislature imposed the levy as a temporary measure pending a more uniform system.
predicates.survey_and_resettlement_were_underway_to: The state was conducting survey and resettlement work to establish uniform land-revenue assessments.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge concerns regional differences in inherited assessments, and a temporary levy applies while survey and resettlement work toward uniform assessments is underway, the rule treats that temporary difference as not violating equality.
